title: The three IDCW options: payout, reinvestment, transfer
objectives: Explain payout, reinvestment and transfer (sweep), and how each is taxed.
Say why reinvestment is usually just the growth option with an extra tax bill.
body_md:
IDCW payout: the payout is credited to the investor's bank account. Units stay the same; NAV falls; cash arrives; taxed at slab rate. IDCW reinvestment: the payout is used to buy more units of the same scheme at the ex-IDCW NAV. More units, same total value — still taxed as if paid out. IDCW transfer (sweep): the payout is invested into another scheme of the same AMC. It moves money between funds and is taxed as a payout.

| Option | What happens | Result for the investor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IDCW payout | Payout is credited to the investor's bank account | Units stay the same; NAV falls; cash arrives; taxed at slab rate |
| IDCW reinvestment | Payout is used to buy more units of the same scheme at the ex-IDCW NAV | More units, same total value; still taxed as if paid out |
| IDCW transfer (sweep) | Payout is invested into another scheme of the same AMC | Moves money between funds; taxed as a payout |

IDCW reinvestment is the least understood. The investor ends up with the same total value as the growth option would have given (before tax), but pays tax on every payout. For most investors who don't need cash, the growth option does the same job without the yearly tax.

> **Investor takeaway:** If you don't need the cash, IDCW reinvestment is usually just the growth option with an extra tax bill.
example: Reinvestment for 8 years: same value as growth before tax, but tax paid on every payout along the way.
say: Reinvestment gives the same value as growth before tax — but with yearly tax.
Transfer moves money between schemes of the same AMC and is taxed as a payout.
never: Reinvestment is the same as an SWP.

check.why: Taxed like a payout. Taxed as if paid out.

check.why: Another scheme of the same AMC. Taxed as a payout.
